questions.q: Which is the correct increasing order of acidic strength?
options: Ethyne < ethanol < phenol < acetic acid < benzenesulphonic acid
Ethanol < ethyne < phenol < acetic acid < benzenesulphonic acid
Ethyne < phenol < ethanol < benzenesulphonic acid < acetic acid
Ethanol < phenol < ethyne < acetic acid < benzenesulphonic acid
questions.explain: pKa values run ethyne (25) > ethanol (16) > phenol (10) > acetic acid (4.76) > sulphonic acid (about −2), so acidity increases in that order.

questions.q: For the equilibrium NaF + HCN ⇌ NaCN + HF, which statement is correct?
options: It lies to the right because CN⁻ is a weaker base than F⁻
It lies to the right with Keq about 10⁶
It lies to the left with Keq about 10⁻⁶, because HF is a much stronger acid than HCN
Keq is close to 1 because both are weak acids
questions.explain: HF (pKa 3.2) is about 10⁶ times stronger than HCN (pKa 9.2), so the proton stays with the weaker acid HCN and the equilibrium favours the left side.

questions.q: Which compound will NOT liberate CO₂ from aqueous NaHCO₃?
questions.explain: NaHCO₃ reacts only with acids stronger than carbonic acid (pKa 6.4). Phenol (pKa 10) is weaker, whereas picric acid (pKa 0.38) is strong enough to react.

questions.q: 5-Sulphosalicylic acid contains –SO₃H, –COOH and a phenolic –OH. After adding exactly 2 equivalents of NaOH, which groups are present in deprotonated form?
questions.explain: Each equivalent of base removes the most acidic remaining proton: first –SO₃H (pKa about −2), then –COOH (4–5); the phenolic OH (about 10) needs a third equivalent.
